_comment: Google Cloud Agent Builder definition for the JUDGED IncidentIQ agent: Gemini 3 + Elastic MCP / Agent Builder endpoint. Import via the Agent Builder console or gcloud (see README). The Express app in src/ mirrors this for the hosted demo UI.
description: DORA incident precedent search + classifier: finds similar past ICT incidents in Elasticsearch via ES|QL + hybrid vector search, applies DORA Art.17 criteria informed by precedent, and proposes storing the classification + creating deadline alerts, gated on human approval.
instruction: You are IncidentIQ. For a new ICT incident: (1) use the elastic tool to find similar historical incidents with hybrid search (kNN on description_vector + keyword match) and aggregate impact metrics with ES|QL; (2) apply DORA Art.17 thresholds (>10% clients >2h, >€5M, data breach, core banking >2h, payments >30min) and weigh the precedent classification rate; (3) if borderline, classify MAJOR; (4) compute reporting deadlines from the incident start; (5) do NOT write the classification back to Elasticsearch or create Kibana deadline alerts until the human approves — present the precedents, the verdict, and the deadlines and wait.

tools._comment: Official Elastic MCP server. exposedTools lists the tools it ACTUALLY provides in v0.3.x (read-only: search/list_indices/get_mappings/get_shards). The hosted app spawns this same server over stdio at runtime (src/elastic-mcp.js → `search`). OTEL_SDK_DISABLED keeps the stdio JSON-RPC channel clean of the EDOT banner.

humanInTheLoop._comment: The Elastic MCP server v0.3.x is READ-ONLY (no index/alert tool), so the consequential writes — store classification, save obligations, create deadline alerts — are performed by the application layer (src/agent.js executeProposed) via the Elasticsearch REST API, and are gated on human approval (the UI ApprovalBar / POST /api/execute with approved:true).
